fix(dedup): solo XML tag lines are fold boundaries unless whole blocks match

The global [×N] line collapse merged open/close tag delimiter lines shared
by structurally distinct blocks (capture 1781260115569010-3cd0e6: two
<task-notification> blocks), deleting the second block's wrappers and
emitting its unique fields as naked sibling XML. Lines that are solely an
XML/HTML open or close tag now carry a block signature (full delimited
block text); delimiters fold only when their entire blocks are
byte-identical, so genuine repeated blocks still collapse whole while every
distinct block keeps its wrapper. Inner non-delimiter lines fold as before.

fix(provider): bullet continuation lines at bullet indentation no longer leak as salient units

Description trim previously segmented column-0 continuation lines after a
bullet as independent sentence units; commit/PR boilerplate then scored max
identifier density and filled the budget while behavioral constraints were
dropped. Now any marker line plus its following non-marker lines (any
indentation, up to the next marker/blank/block boundary) form one item unit,
scored on the marker line only; when the whole item does not fit, the marker
line alone is emitted (sentence-trimmed if needed) with an elision marker.
Marker scoring is structural: call-signature-shaped markers rank as payload
with fences; an all-caps admonition label (IMPORTANT:, WARNING:) ranks above
plain units; otherwise identifier density as before.

fix: never elide test/build failures during pruning (TAP not-ok drop)

A TAP log (node --test, prove) could lose its only failing test: the
STRONG failure regex didn't know TAP's 'not ok' marker or camelCase
diagnostics like failureType: 'testCodeFailure', and the retrieve stage
selected chunks purely by query relevance — a failure rarely shares
words with 'run the tests', so it was elided along with '# fail 1'.

- retrieve: failure-signal chunks plus their continuation blocks
  (indented traceback frames; for TAP, the whole YAML diagnostic up to
  the next test point) are force-kept in every selection path, at both

fix: detect tool re-runs through run-to-run noise (masked fingerprint)

The repeat→passthrough rail compared raw text, so a re-run whose output
differed only in volatile values (TAP duration_ms, timestamps, ports,
PIDs) never matched — the retry was windowed identically and the agent
could never recover elided detail, exactly the loop the elision header
promises can't happen.

Repeat detection now hashes each line's template_of() mask (numbers,
hex, UUIDs, timestamps, IPs -> {}), so timing-only re-runs pass through
in full while a real result change (ok <-> not ok) still compresses
fresh. A masked false match only ships one output uncompressed.

  works around a maturin 1.14 / uniffi 0.31 packaging gap (auto mode ships an

  wheel with valid RECORD hashes.

fix(tools): prune tools only on the first turn to keep the cache prefix stable (#9) (#11)

Tool selection keeps only the tools its relevance ranking scores against the
conversation, so the kept subset changes turn-to-turn. Providers fold the
`tools[]` block into the cached prompt prefix, so a changing block invalidates
the prefix on every turn of an agent loop: provider prompt-cache reads collapse
and the prefix is rebilled as fresh input — which on a cache-warm loop costs
more than not compressing at all (issue #9).

Gate `select_tools` to the first turn of a conversation: at most one non-system
message and no tool invoked yet (`is_first_turn`, cross-wire-shape over
messages / input / contents, with a tools-used-in-history loop guard that now
also covers the Responses `input[]` `function_call` shape). There the saving is
free — no prior prefix to bust — while from the second turn on the tool set is
left intact and only the deterministic trim/minify stages shrink the block,
keeping it byte-identical turn to turn. Applies to every preset that selects
tools (agent, aggressive, both of which also enable the cache stage).

The former "keep already-invoked tools" rail is removed: selection now only runs
on the first turn, where no tool has been invoked, so it was unreachable.

This supersedes an earlier attempt that made selection monotonic over the whole
conversation: live testing on gpt-4o-mini showed the churn is growth-driven and a
growing block still busts the cache, so only first-turn pruning is cache-safe.

Tests: end-to-end byte-stability across two mid-loop turns under the agent preset;
first-turn detection across OpenAI Chat / Responses, Anthropic, and Gemini shapes;
multi-turn selection is skipped.

fix(setup): bypass localhost/LAN with NO_PROXY and self-heal old installs (#56)

Wiring HTTPS_PROXY for the whole user routed *every* proxy-aware program's
local and LAN traffic at the interceptor, not just LLM tools. When the
interceptor was down or on a stale port, those calls failed with "couldn't
connect" -- e.g. Plex device discovery, localhost dev servers, intranet hosts.

The managed env block (and HKCU\Environment on Windows) now also exports
NO_PROXY/no_proxy -- both casings, since curl and Go only read the lowercase
form -- covering localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, *.local, and the private LAN
ranges. The literal hosts and *.local are honored by nearly every client;
CIDR-based LAN bypass is best-effort (curl and Node/undici match only by exact
host or domain suffix, not CIDR). llmtrim only MITMs a fixed set of public LLM
API hosts (the CA's domain set), so local/LAN hosts were never intercepted --
the bypass changes nothing for compression, it just stops a dead proxy from
breaking unrelated traffic.

Existing installs self-heal: the supervised daemon rewrites a pre-NO_PROXY
managed block in place when it starts at login, reusing the wired port, so no
`setup` re-run is needed. The heal is scoped to a well-formed BEGIN..END block
that lacks the bypass (a malformed or already-current block is left untouched,
and a user's own NO_PROXY outside the markers does not mask a stale block).
Already-running apps still need a one-time restart to pick up the new env.

fix(serve): fail fast on a busy port, add --force to replace a daemon (#70)

`serve --supervised` treated a bind failure as a transient crash and spun
through the restart loop five times before giving up, even though the port
being in use is permanent. Pre-flight the port: if a live llmtrim daemon
already holds it, refuse with an actionable message (`llmtrim stop` first,
or `--force` to replace it); if a foreign process holds it, say so. Only an
in-use bind error maps to PortInUse (non-transient → the supervisor surfaces
it once instead of retrying); a permission/transient bind error keeps its OS
cause and stays retryable.

`--force` on `serve`, `start`, and `setup` stops the existing daemon first
(via the guarded `daemon::stop`, which never kills a foreign process), waits
for the port to actually free (shared `daemon::stop_and_wait_free`), then
takes over. In the supervised loop `--force` applies only to the first start,
never to a crash-restart.

Daemon liveness (`daemon::running`) now also verifies the pid is llmtrim, not
just that some process has it, so a stale pidfile naming a recycled pid is
cleared rather than mistaken for a running daemon (which `--force` would then
try to stop).

the terse/draft prose instruction is gated behind an explicit

compression, no terse) for clean benchmarking. Prompt text is

provider prefix cache (~57% of grok turns on measured captures).

mid-session and breaking cache at byte 0 even when history was stable.

- first-write-wins put() so discarded freezes cannot poison the store
- sticky envelope restore on memo hit
- serve: never drop a memo hit to chase a slightly smaller fresh body

  edit invalidation, and unforwarded-body poisoning
